subject: [Retro Lab] Open actions — Sprint 3 Retro (Sprint 3)
body:
Sprint 3 Retro
Period: Sprint 3
Team: Chartswap
Archived: October 14, 2026
Open approved actions (4):
• ACT-0001 — Cap the code review queue and agree first-response norms
  Teams: Dev Team, Management Team | Target: 2026-10-14
  The team reported reviews backing up when too many pull requests wait at once (FB-0003). A shared WIP limit per reviewer and a first-response target should keep the queue moving without blaming individuals.
• ACT-0002 — Expand regression and integration coverage in the delivery pipeline
  Teams: Dev Team, QA Team | Target: 2026-10-14
  Recurring feedback pointed to gaps in regression and integration testing before release (FB-0004, FB-0005). The team can prioritize high-risk flows, add automated checks where practical, and define what must pass before merge or deploy.
• ACT-0003 — Add a pre-deploy deployment configuration validation step
  Teams: Ops Team, Dev Team | Target: 2026-10-14
  The team flagged environment or deployment configuration issues surfacing late (FB-0006). A short checklist or automated diff against known-good settings before promote should catch misconfigurations earlier.
• ACT-0004 — Standardize refinement handoffs and keep QA involved early
  Teams: Product Team, QA Team, Dev Team | Target: 2026-10-14
  The team valued QA participation during refinement (FB-0001) while handoffs between roles still felt unclear (FB-0002). Agree on ready-for-dev criteria, who owns the handoff, and a lightweight refinement template so expectations stay visible.
Themes: Early quality involvement in planning: The team noted that QA participation in refinement helped surface missing acceptance criteria before implementation work progressed. Cross-team delivery handoffs: A recurring positive theme is smoother coordination between backend and frontend during the sprint. Code review throughput: The team reported that the code review queue expanded again during the middle of the sprint. Integration testing and regression risk: Process feedback links a shipped regression to gaps in integration coverage, and the team explicitly called for broader integration tests around payment flows. Deployment pipeline safeguards: The team suggested strengthening the deployment path by automating configuration validation.
—
